subject: biology
topic: Cell structure, organelles and levels of organisation

kept.q: Which pair of cell organelles is correctly described as being bounded by a double membrane envelope?
options: Mitochondrion and chloroplast
Golgi apparatus and lysosome
Ribosome and centriole
Vacuole and peroxisome
kept.explanation: Mitochondria and chloroplasts both have an outer and inner membrane, unlike Golgi bodies, lysosomes, ribosomes and vacuoles which are single-membraned or have no membrane at all.
kept.pidgin: Mitochondria and chloroplast get double membrane wey dey cover dem. Other organelles like Golgi body or ribosome no get double membrane like dat.

kept.q: A tissue is defined in biology as
options: a single cell specialized to carry out one specific function
a group of similar cells working together to perform a particular function
different organs working together to form a complete body system
a collection of unrelated cells randomly grouped within an organism
kept.explanation: A tissue is made up of similar cells that have the same origin and structure and that work together to perform a common function, such as muscle tissue contracting to produce movement.
kept.pidgin: Tissue na group of cells wey get same shape and work together to do one particular job. Like muscle tissue, dem dey work together to make body move.

kept.q: Which of the following best explains why plant cells generally do not burst when placed in distilled water, while animal cells placed in the same solution may burst?
options: Plant cells lack a nucleus to regulate water intake
Plant cells have a rigid cellulose cell wall that resists excess water pressure
Plant cells have smaller vacuoles that cannot take in water
Plant cells actively pump out all water entering by osmosis
kept.explanation: The cellulose cell wall of a plant cell provides mechanical support against the internal pressure created as water enters by osmosis, preventing bursting. Animal cells lack this wall, so they can swell and burst in a hypotonic solution.
kept.pidgin: Plant cell get strong cellulose cell wall wey dey hold am make e no burst when water enter. Animal cell no get that wall, so e fit burst if water too much.

kept.q: A thin, folded network of membranes studded with ribosomes extends from the nuclear envelope throughout the cytoplasm of a secretory cell. This structure most likely functions to
options: synthesize and transport proteins for secretion
generate ATP through oxidative phosphorylation
digest worn-out organelles using hydrolytic enzymes
store starch grains for later use by the cell
kept.explanation: A membrane network studded with ribosomes is the rough endoplasmic reticulum, which synthesizes proteins at the ribosomes and channels them through its lumen for packaging and secretion.
kept.pidgin: That network wey get ribosome na rough endoplasmic reticulum. E dey use ribosome make protein and carry am go where e suppose go.

kept.q: Which of the following is a major structural feature distinguishing prokaryotic cells from eukaryotic cells?
options: Prokaryotic cells have a true membrane-bound nucleus while eukaryotic cells do not
Prokaryotic cells lack membrane-bound organelles while eukaryotic cells possess them
Prokaryotic cells contain mitochondria while eukaryotic cells rely only on the cell membrane for respiration
Prokaryotic cells have a cellulose cell wall while eukaryotic cells never have a cell wall
kept.explanation: Prokaryotic cells such as bacteria have no membrane-bound nucleus or organelles like mitochondria and Golgi bodies, whereas eukaryotic cells possess these structures enclosed by their own membranes.
kept.pidgin: Prokaryotic cells no get membrane-bound organelles like mitochondria or nucleus. Eukaryotic cells get all those organelles inside dem.

kept.q: A student views a specimen under the light microscope using a x10 eyepiece lens and a x40 objective lens. What is the total magnification of the image observed?
options: x4
kept.explanation: Total magnification is found by multiplying the eyepiece magnification by the objective magnification, so 10 multiplied by 40 gives 400.
kept.pidgin: To get total magnification, you go multiply eyepiece lens by objective lens. So, 10 times 40 give you 400.

kept.q: In an investigation, a scientist isolates an organelle from liver cells and finds that it contains hydrolytic (digestive) enzymes capable of breaking down worn-out organelles and foreign materials engulfed by the cell. This organelle is most likely the
options: Golgi apparatus
smooth endoplasmic reticulum
lysosome
peroxisome
kept.explanation: Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes that digest worn-out organelles, cell debris and foreign particles taken into the cell, a process important in cellular maintenance and defense. The other organelles listed do not primarily function in intracellular digestion.
kept.pidgin: Lysosome na the organelle wey get digestive enzymes to break down old parts of cell. E dey help cell clean im body and fight foreign things.

q.q: Four organisms are arranged below according to increasing organisational complexity: a single amoeba living independently, a colony of cells forming a simple sponge, a tissue layer lining the human gut, and a complete human digestive system made up of several organs. Which of the following correctly ranks these from the simplest to the most complex level of organisation?
options: Tissue layer, amoeba, digestive system, sponge colony
Amoeba, sponge colony, tissue layer, digestive system
Digestive system, tissue layer, sponge colony, amoeba
Sponge colony, digestive system, amoeba, tissue layer
q.explanation: A single-celled amoeba represents the cellular level, a sponge colony represents a loose grouping of cells, a tissue layer represents true tissue organisation, and a full digestive system represents organ-system level, so the correct order from simplest to most complex is amoeba, sponge colony, tissue layer, digestive system.
